children: EQT is buying local rival Range Resources to create a US leader. Cost savings won’t cover the 21% premium being paid, but boss Toby Rice sees more. Although Appalachian producers must export, data centers are spurring local demand, auguring higher production and, perhaps, prices.
Full view will be published shortly.

EQT said on October 26 it agreed to buy rival natural gas producer Range Resources for nearly $13 billion in an all-stock deal. Range investors will receive 0.987 shares of EQT for each share held. That is a 21% premium to where Range's stock closed on October 23, the last day of trading before the deal was announced. EQT investors will own 73% of the combined company.
The deal creates the largest US natural gas company, with 9 billion cubic feet equivalent of production per day, and more than 30 years of inventory.
